purpose: reader-facing explanation of AI Engineering responsibilities, organizational settings, and core skills

required_facts.fact: An AI Engineer integrates AI into a product and keeps the system reliable, evaluated, maintained, and improved.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 45: the role definition is stated.

required_facts.fact: The role translates product requirements into scoped AI problems and selects appropriate models and tools.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 50-53: problem and integration responsibilities are listed.

required_facts.fact: Prompt versioning, success metrics, comprehensive tests, deployment, monitoring, cost optimization, and security are included.
Unlike a typical data-science or ML-engineering distinction, AI Engineering often uses third-party foundation models through APIs.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 61-65: model-provider context and role distinction are explained.

required_facts.fact: AI Engineering work may be distributed across data scientists, ML engineers, and software engineers in organizations with established ML teams.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 70-75: distributed responsibility is described.

required_facts.fact: Dedicated AI Engineers may sit in product engineering, centralized AI platform, or applied ML groups.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 75: dedicated-role settings are listed.

required_facts.fact: Startups often use a product-focused generalist who moves from experimentation to production hardening.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 77: startup role shape is stated.

required_facts.fact: RAG skill includes ingestion, chunking, embeddings, semantic search, and grounded response generation.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 85-89: RAG pipeline components are specified.

required_facts.fact: Agentic skill includes function calling, structured tools, MCP integration, and reasoning flows for tool use.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 91-95: agentic-system components are described.

required_facts.fact: Evaluation and observability include real-input tests, datasets, quality metrics, logging, failure tracking, dashboards, and quality-drift analysis.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 97-107: evaluation and monitoring practices are listed.

author_attribution: Explain the responsibilities and skills as Alexey's documented perspective, retaining the qualification that organizational maturity changes the role.
